package_info.why_malicious: The Orion Platform software updates were compromised during the SolarWinds build process, resulting in the distribution of digitally signed binaries containing the SUNBURST backdoor. This allowed attackers to covertly gain persistent, unauthorized access to customer environments through trusted software supply chain updates.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Malicious DLL injected into SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (SUNBURST):
- On initialization, the DLL checks for specific system characteristics (e.g., domain, running processes, security tools) to evade sandboxes and security analysis.
- It delays execution for up to two weeks to avoid detection.
- It establishes a DNS-based command-and-control (C2) channel to avsvmcloud[.]com, using custom-encoded subdomains to communicate with attacker infrastructure.
- It retrieves and executes attacker-supplied commands, including file transfer, process execution, system profiling, and lateral movement.
- It uses legitimate Orion Platform service startup for persistence.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C# (compiled to DLL, loaded by Orion Platform EXE)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (service startup), the malicious DLL performs anti-analysis checks and delays execution, then initiates DNS-based C2 communication to avsvmcloud[.]com using encoded subdomains, receives attacker instructions, and executes remote commands for data exfiltration and lateral movement, resulting in persistent unauthorized access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes covert external network connections to an attacker-controlled domain (avsvmcloud[.]com) at service startup, employs anti-analysis and execution delay techniques, and enables remote command execution—all of which are highly atypical for legitimate monitoring software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion Platform DLLs should not initiate outbound DNS queries to untrusted or obfuscated domains, should not execute remote commands, and should not contain anti-analysis or execution delay logic.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may check for updates or license validation, but these actions are typically performed over HTTPS to trusted vendor domains, not via obfuscated DNS C2 to unknown infrastructure, nor with anti-analysis or execution delay logic.
key_indicators: Obfuscated DNS queries to avsvmcloud[.]com with custom-encoded subdomains
Remote command execution capability via attacker-supplied payloads
Anti-analysis checks (e.g., process, domain, and security tool detection)
Execution delay logic (up to two weeks) to evade detection
Persistence via legitimate Orion service startup

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the Orion Platform build process, resulting in digitally signed, tainted binaries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of compromised software updates to SolarWinds customers

attack_chain.action: Customers install or update to the compromised Orion Platform versions, deploying the malicious DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the SUNBURST backdoor on customer systems

attack_chain.action: The malicious DLL performs anti-analysis checks and delays execution, then initiates DNS-based C2 communication to avsvmcloud[.]com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker establishes covert remote access to the environment

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues commands for data exfiltration, lateral movement, and further compromise via the C2 channel.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise and persistent unauthorized access to customer environment

behavioral_signatures: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll loaded at service startup initiates outbound DNS queries to avsvmcloud[.]com with custom-encoded subdomains
Unexpected network activity (DNS or HTTP) from Orion Platform processes to untrusted domains
Presence of anti-analysis or execution delay logic in Orion DLLs
Remote command execution or process spawning by Orion Platform services
network_indicators: DNS queries to avsvmcloud[.]com and related subdomains
Subsequent C2 traffic to attacker-controlled infrastructure (e.g., secondary domains/IPs resolved from avsvmcloud[.]com)
Encoded data in DNS query subdomains from Orion Platform hosts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Orion Platform binaries matching known malicious hashes or affected versions. Inspect DNS logs for queries to avsvmcloud[.]com or related subdomains originating from Orion Platform hosts. Use EDR or network monitoring to detect DLLs with anti-analysis or execution delay logic, and to identify remote command execution or process spawning by Orion services. Correlate software deployment logs to identify systems that received tainted updates.
